conclusion.justification: The report explicitly states that scientific evidence generally supports the claim that opening a bedroom window or door improves sleep quality, citing improved ventilation, lower carbon dioxide levels, and increased sleep efficiency.
conclusion.label: endorses

report:
Contrary to your initial assumption, scientific evidence generally **supports** the claim that opening a bedroom window or door improves sleep quality. 

During the night, human breathing causes carbon dioxide ($\text{CO}_2$) to build up in closed rooms. Research demonstrates that opening bedroom windows or doors enhances ventilation, lowering $\text{CO}_2$ concentrations and improving indoor air quality. This improved air flow is associated with increased sleep efficiency, greater amounts of deep sleep, fewer nighttime awakenings, and better next-day cognitive performance [https://www.sci.news/medicine/opening-windows-doors-sleep-quality-05459.html, https://www.psypost.org/enhanced-bedroom-ventilation-linked-to-improved-sleep-quality/].

Studies evaluating specific ventilation methods note that opening a window—bringing in fresh outdoor air—is especially effective at increasing air freshness and supporting sleep quality, whereas opening an interior door alone may have a more limited effect [https://waseda.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/the-effects-of-bedroom-windowdoor-opening-on-bedroom-air-quality-].

The primary caveat to this claim involves environmental factors: opening a window does not filter out external fine particulate matter or gaseous air pollutants, and it can expose sleepers to outdoor noise, both of which can reduce sleep quality if local conditions are poor [https://healthyairtech.com/news/opening-a-window-does-not-stop-air-pollution/]. 

In conclusion, unless outdoor noise or air pollution is an issue, the evidence indicates that ventilating a bedroom by opening a window or door beneficial for sleep.

**Sources:**
* https://www.sci.news/medicine/opening-windows-doors-sleep-quality-05459.html
* https://www.psypost.org/enhanced-bedroom-ventilation-linked-to-improved-sleep-quality/
* https://waseda.elsevierpure.com/en/publications/the-effects-of-bedroom-windowdoor-opening-on-bedroom-air-quality-
* https://healthyairtech.com/news/opening-a-window-does-not-stop-air-pollution/
